name: Function
first: A named block of code that takes inputs and can return a value.

what.is: A function is a block of code with a name. You declare it once, with `func`, and run it by calling its name. It can take inputs, called parameters, and it can return a value.
what.afterExample: Lines 1 to 3 declare a function named `greet`. Line 4 calls it, and `message` holds the value that it returns.
what.problem: The same work is often needed in more than one place, with different values. A function lets you write that work once, and run it from each place with the values that place gives it.
what.how: Declaring `greet` does not run its body. The call on line 4 runs the body, with the parameter `name` set to the argument `"Ana"`. The call ends at `return`, and gives back the value after it.

when.text: Use one when the same work is needed in more than one place, or when a piece of work has one job that you can name. Each call runs the same body with its own argument:

Don't use one when the code is handed to another function to run, such as the code that `map` runs once for each item. There, write a closure instead: a function with no name, written right where it is handed over.

parts.name: `func`
parts.text: The word `func` starts the declaration of a function, on line 1.

parts.name: The name, `greet`
parts.text: `greet` is the function's name. A call uses this name to run the function, as line 4 does.

parts.name: The parameter list, `(name: String)`
parts.text: The inputs that the function takes, in parentheses. `name` is a parameter, and `String` is its type. Inside the body, `name` holds the value that the call gave it.

parts.name: The return type, `-> String`
parts.text: The type of the value that the function gives back. `greet` gives back a `String`.

parts.name: The body
parts.text: The code between `{` on line 1 and `}` on line 3. It runs each time the function is called.

parts.name: `return`
parts.text: `return` on line 2 ends the call, and gives back the value after it. That value must have the return type, `String`.

parts.name: The call, on line 4
parts.text: Line 4 calls `greet`. In the parentheses, `name:` is the argument label: it says which parameter the value is for. `"Ana"` is the argument: the value that the parameter `name` gets. Its type must be the parameter's type, `String`.

steps.text: The body runs, with `name` set to `"Ana"`. Line 2 returns the string "Hello, Ana", and the call ends.
Line 4 stores the returned string in `message`.

end.text: `greet` runs only when it is called. Each call gives `name` the argument of that call, and gives back the value after `return`.
